The present writ petition has been filed for issuance of show cause t
respondents as to how and under what authority, the construction work was started over the
petitioners' raiyati land appertaining to Plot No. 380, Khata No. 69, Mouza-Haratu, P.S-Namkum,
District-Ranchi, measuring an area of 24 Decimals without following due procedure of acquisition.

Further prayer has been made for issuance of direction upon the respondents to compensate the petitioners under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition (Rehabilitation and Resettlement) Act, 2013 in lieu of illegal construction made over the said land.

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners are the bonafide owners of the said land which was purchased by them way back in the year 1981 & 1982 by way of registered sale deed and hence they cannot be deprived of compensation by the respondent authorities for unlawful acquisition of the same.

3. A counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of the respondent Nos. 1 to 3 stating inter alia that when the petitioners applied under the Right to Information Act, 2005 to obtain the documents relating to the land in question, the same were not available in the office of the Divisional Railway Manager, Ranchi, however, later on, those documents were obtained.

From perusal of the said documents, it would be evident that the same relate to acquisition of the land in question by the State Government for construction of double-track railway line between Muri and Hatia in L. A.
Case No. 63 of 1974-75 which was handed over to railway on 21.03.1983.
4.

Another counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of the respondent No.6 stating that 0.58 Acre land appertaining to Plot No. 380, Khata No. 69 of Village- Haratu as well as other lands were acquired by the erstwhile State of Bihar vide L. A. Case No. 05/1962-63 pursuant to Memorandum of Agreement entered between the erstwhile State of Bihar and Damodar Valley Refractories (Pvt.)
Limited, Calcutta for establishment of a factory vide notification dated 10.04.1962 published in the Bihar Gazette dated 11.04.1962 whereas the land measuring an area of 0.24 Acre, out of 0.58 Acre,
Plot No. 380 of the said Mouza as well as other lands of adjoining villages belonging to Damodar Valley Refractories (Pvt.) Ltd. was acquired by the then District Land Acquisition Officer, Ranchi vide L. A. Case No. 63/1974-75 for construction of double-track railway line from Hatia to Muri.
The writ petition has been filed after considerable delay i.e. after more than four decades and hence on this score alone, the same is liable to be dismissed.
5. It has also been stated that an award for Rs.9,720.95 was prepared in favour of Damodar Valley Refractories (Pvt.) Ltd.

Thereafter, the Director of Damodar Valley Refractories (Pvt.) Ltd. received the awarded amount on 11.10.1977 which is evident from consolidated Voucher available in the office of the concerned respondent.
The possession of land was delivered to the Dy. Chief Engineer (C), Railway, Ranchi vide certificate of possession dated 21.03.1983.
Subsequently, the map of the acquired lands was prepared.

So far as the rest part of 0.34 Acre of land, out of 0.58 Acre land belonging to the Damodar Valley Refractories (Pvt.) Ltd. is concerned, since the said Company did not use the acquired land, the erstwhile Government of Bihar reclaimed the said land and took possession of the same which was later on transferred to Ranchi Industrial Area Development Authority (now Jharkhand Industrial Area Development Authority).
6.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and considering the aforesaid statements made in the counter affidavits filed on behalf of the respondent Nos. 1 to 3 as well as the respondent No.6, it appears that the acquisition proceeding with respect to the land in question as well as other lands was initiated in phase wise manner from 1962-63 and the part of the said land was handed over to railway on 21.03.1983 for construction of double-track railway line from Hatia to Muri which is in operation for years together.
Moreover, the part of the said land was reclaimed by the erstwhile State of Bihar several years back.
Hence, the petitioners have failed to make out any case for payment of compensation for the land in question.
